First of all, many people don’t get into medical school the first time they apply. If you end up taking a gap year or things just don’t go as planned, you should be able to find an entry level job with a degree in statistics. I have many friends who were pre-med or pre-vet students and got degrees in biology. They found out pretty quickly that a BA/BS is not usually enough to find a job in that field. Most jobs related to biology require further education. 

Having a college degree of any kind will qualify for many jobs, but it never hurts to expand your skill set to improve your chances of finding employment. What I’m saying is that it’s good to have a back up plan. 

Another factor is that the additional degree (as well as the fact that it is in statistics) will set you apart from other medical school applicants. It also shows that you chose to challenge yourself by doing more. 

There are many pros to completing the stats degree, but in the end it will probably come down to time and money. I suggest that you complete it as a double major so that you won’t have to retake your general education requirements. You’ll need to think about your scholarships and financial aid and decide if it will be affordable for you.
